summary: Several cantons allow voters to recall a cantonal authority or parliament before the end of its term through a citizen petition and vote.
Recall of state and local officials is permitted in 19 states. California's statewide gubernatorial recalls are among the most well known examples.
The Recall and Initiative Act (1995) lets voters petition to remove a Member of the Legislative Assembly between elections.
The Recall of MPs Act (2015) can trigger a by-election when an MP meets specific conditions and enough constituents sign a recall petition.
Several states allow the recall of mayors and local councils through citizen petitions followed by a local referendum.
Recall provisions already exist in municipal and panchayat laws in states such as Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Bihar for certain local representatives.
